newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks off in London after U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks off in London after U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Japanese stocks met renewed selling pressure in London in mid-afternoon trading on Friday after a stronger-than-expected set of U.S. employment data fanned fears of a near-term U.S. interest rate hike, dealers said.
By 1443 GMT, the Nikkei 50 average was down 54.03 points in London to 1,302.96, the lowest level since December 1995.

Battered Japanese shares stabilised in London in early trading amid light bargain hunting, dealers said. Bank issues, like Fuji Bank and Sakura Bank, which have been particularly hard hit during the past week, were the focus of buying interest, they said.
"But once those (U.S. jobs) figures came out, everything changed," said one London broker. "They're hitting Wall Street and that's hitting us."
The Dow sank at the open, and was down 62.34 points, or almost one percent, to 6,563.33 by 1443 GMT. Wall Street's losses dragged down most European borses, as well.
In Tokyo, the benchmark Nikkei 225 average shed 770.22 points, or 4.26 percent, to settle at 17,303.65. It was lowest close since August 1995 and the biggest one-day loss in two years.
